item.title: Eastern North Pacific Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
000
ABPZ20 KNHC 022308
TWOEP

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
500 PM PDT Wed Sep 2 2026

For the eastern and central North Pacific east of 180 longitude:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Hurricane
Karina, located well east of the Hawaiian Islands, on Hurricane
Lowell, located several hundred miles south of the Hawaiian Islands,
and on Tropical Storm Marie, located several hundred miles
south-southwest of the southern tip of the Baja California
Peninsula.

Offshore of Southwestern Mexico:
An area of low pressure could form well offshore of southwestern
Mexico over the weekend or early next week. Gradual development is
possible during the early to middle part of next week as the system
moves west-northwestward at 10 to 15 mph, and is likely to remain
well offshore of Mexico.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...near 0 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...low...30 percent.

$$
Forecaster Evans/Hagen

MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...947 MB...27.97 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 500 PM HST (0300 UTC), the center of Hurricane Karina was located 
near latitude 19.3 North, longitude 134.7 West. Karina is moving 
toward the west-northwest near 10 mph (17 km/h) and a 
west-northwestward motion is expected over the next few days.
 
Maximum sustained winds are near 130 mph (215 km/h) with higher 
gusts.  Karina is a category 4 hurricane on the Saffir-Simpson 
Hurricane Wind Scale.  A slow weakening trend is forecast the next 
few days, followed by a more steady rate of weakening. Karina is 
likely to remain a hurricane the next couple of days.
 
Hurricane-force winds extend outward up to 35 miles (55 km) from the
center and tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 125 miles
(205 km).
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 947 mb (27.97 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
None.

-------------

item.title: Hurricane Karina Forecast Discussion Number 26
item.description:
Issued at 1100 AM HST Wed Sep 02 2026 
000
WTPZ41 KNHC 022033
TCDEP1
 
Hurricane Karina Discussion Number  26
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP112026
1100 AM HST Wed Sep 02 2026
 
Karina's satellite presentation has degraded this morning,
characterized by warming cloud tops in infrared imagery and an eye
that has become more cloud-filled. The system is still annular,
although there are signs of the system losing that structure in
recent microwave imagery that depicts the eastern eyewall has
started to thin. The Data T-number from the latest TAFB Dvorak
classification has decreased to T5.5, with a Current Intensity (CI)
of 6.5. Objective intensity estimates have also been gradually
decreasing since the previous advisory and currently range from 112
to 127 kt. Given the degraded satellite appearance and a blend of
the available intensity estimates, the initial intensity is set to
120 kt for this advisory, which could be a little generous.
 
The steering pattern is well established, and a westward to
west-northwestward motion is anticipated over the next several days
while the system is steered by a subtropical ridge to its north.
Later in the forecast period, a mid-level low is forecast to move
into the central Pacific north of the Hawaiian Islands. This feature
will cause the ridge to weaken, inducing a more northwestward turn.
The latest NHC track forecast is very similar to the previous one
and is based on a blend of the HCCA and GDMI consensus aids.
 
Karina will track over marginally warm sea surface temperatures over 
the next few days with low wind shear. However, the system will be 
moving into a drier, more stable airmass by tomorrow. This should 
induce a gradual weakening trend during the next day or so. Wind 
shear is than expected to increase, combined with the track moving 
over cooler SSTs by 72 h, which will result in a more steady rate of 
weakening. The NHC intensity forecast remains on the higher end of 
the intensity guidance in the near term, given the still annular 
structure, followed by a faster rate closer to some of the consensus 
intensity aids. By Day 5, the system is forecast to become 
post-tropical as models show the system becoming devoid of 
convection.

NORTHWESTWARD WELL OFFSHORE OF THE MEXICAN COAST...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 200 PM MST...2100 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...18.0N 112.5W
ABOUT 380 MI...610 KM SSW OF THE SOUTHERN TIP OF BAJA CALIFORNIA
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...70 MPH...110 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...NW OR 310 DEGREES AT 12 MPH...19 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...992 MB...29.30 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 200 PM MST (2100 UTC), the center of Tropical Storm Marie was 
located near latitude 18.0 North, longitude 112.5 West. Marie is 
moving toward the northwest near 12 mph (19 km/h). This motion 
should continue through tonight followed by a turn more 
west-northwestward for the next several days.
 
Maximum sustained winds are near 70 mph (110 km/h) with higher 
gusts. Additional strengthening is forecast through Friday, and 
Marie is likely to become a hurricane tonight. Gradual weakening is 
anticipated to begin by this weekend.
 
Tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 185 miles (295 km)
from the center.
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 992 mb (29.30 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
SURF: Swells generated by Marie will affect portions of the coast of
southwest Mexico and the Baja California Peninsula for the next few
days and will likely spread northward to southern California over
the weekend.  These swells are likely to cause life-threatening surf
and rip current conditions. Please consult products from your local
weather office. A depiction of rip current risk for the United
States can be found at:
hurricanes.gov/graphics_ep1.shtml?ripCurrents
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 800 PM MST.
 
$$
Forecaster Papin

item.title: Tropical Storm Marie Forecast Discussion Number 7
item.description:
Issued at 200 PM MST Wed Sep 02 2026 
000
WTPZ43 KNHC 022042
TCDEP3
 
Tropical Storm Marie Discussion Number   7
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP132026
200 PM MST Wed Sep 02 2026
 
Since the previous advisory, Marie has experienced bit of a hiccup
in its convective structure, with warming clouds tops near the
center aside from a recent burst wrapping around west of the
center. The most recent microwave pass from this morning showed a
banding type eye attempting to form, though it was struggling to
close off on its northwest side. In addition, there was an RCM-3
SAR pass earlier today with an interesting structure, showing a
small core, but with stronger winds occuring along the outer bands
of Marie's circulation. This structure hints that it might take
some time for the inner-core to fully consolidate. For now, the
18 UTC TAFB Dvorak satellite estimate was T3.5/55 kt, while the
objective intensity estimates range from 53 to 67 kt. Thus, the
initial intensity will remain 60 kt this advisory, keeping Marie
just shy of hurricane intensity.
 
Marie appears to be a little right of the prior forecast track, but
is still moving off to the northwest, with the estimated motion at
310/10 kt. Over the next several days, a narrow mid-level ridge
located to the north and northeast is expected to steer the tropical
cyclone generally off to the west-northwest, gradually slowing its
forward motion in the process as the ridge slowly weakens. Beyond 60
h, there continues to be significant cross-track spread that
develops among the model guidance, related to how much an amplified
mid-latitude trough, off the western United States coast, erodes
this ridge. For this cycle, some of the more reliable track aids,
ECMWF, Google DeepMind (GDMI), HCCA, actually show Marie turning
back westward in the day 4-5 time frame, as the ridge holds to the
north of the cyclone while the mid-latitude trough moves inland over
the western United States. However, there remain a minority of
solutions that show a more rightward track if the trough fully
erodes the ridge steering Marie. The NHC track forecast this cycle
is slightly right of the prior one for the first 48-60 h, following
the latest trends in the GDMI and HCCA aids, but now bends a little
more westward in days 4-5, also following trends in these aids.
 
Intensity-wise, the earlier SAR imagery in addition to a partial
ASCAT-C pass show Marie has a broad wind field with a
larger-than-normal radius of maximum wind. This could prevent more
rapid development over the next couple of days despite the favorable
environmental conditions. Thereafter, while sea-surface
temperatures (SSTs), diagnosed by SHIPS guidance between 27-28 C,
appear favorable, some of these waters were recently churned up by
the last tropical cyclone along this track (Iselle last week), and
the HAFS-A/B hurricane-regional models suggest the large wind field
of Marie could upwell some cooler waters underneath. Thus the latest
NHC intensity forecast shows a somewhat lower intensity than
earlier, peaking at 80 kt in the day 2-3 time frame. This intensity
forecast favors the hurricane-regional models over the latest SHIPS
guidance given the potential for ocean upwelling. Marie should be
crossing the 26 C SST isotherm after 72 h, and weakening is expected
to begin in earnest beyond this time period.
